typography.usage: Use 'Caveat' for primary game titles, win/lose messaging, and hand-written aesthetics. Import them from Google Fonts in index.css. Use 'Space Mono' for scoreboards, turn indicators, and technical game UI elements to simulate a typewriter or technical draft feel. Avoid Inter or standard sans-serifs completely.

colors.usage_rules: Theme is physical/analog. Backgrounds for UI panels (modals, scoreboards) MUST be parchment/paper colored (#F5F2EB). Text must replicate ballpoint pen ink (#141E50 for blue, #B42828 for red). Never use pure black or sterile grays. Shadows should be warm dark brown (#2A1A12) with varying opacity.

visual_enhancers.surfaces: Diegetic UI: Menus and modals MUST look like notebook paper, index cards, or masking tape sitting on the desk. Apply heavy drop shadows, e.g., 'shadow-[4px_8px_16px_rgba(20,10,0,0.6)]' to lift paper off the wood background.
visual_enhancers.borders: Avoid perfectly smooth borders. Use 2px solid '#141E50' to look drawn, or rely on actual paper textures. You can use CSS border-radius irregularities (e.g., 'rounded-[2px_255px_3px_255px]') to simulate hand-cut paper.
visual_enhancers.textures: Overlay a subtle noise texture or use the provided ruled paper image for modals. Never use glassmorphism; it breaks the physical, tactile illusion.

grids.modes: MODE A: Asymmetrical layout for the Main Menu to simulate papers casually tossed on a desk. Do not perfectly center-align everything; use subtle rotations (e.g., -rotate-1 or rotate-2).
grids.gaps: Use wide gaps (gap-8 to gap-12) to give the UI breathing room over the dense wood background.

layouts.spacing: Generous spacing. Modals should be padded heavily (p-8 to p-12).
layouts.positioning: HUD elements (Turn Indicator, Scoreboard) must be pinned to the screen corners (absolute positioning). They should look like taped notes attached to the desk surface. Mute button can look like a small pin or drawn icon in the top-right.

component_rules.MenuScreen: A large 'notebook page' modal centered over the dark wood background. Include the game title in a massive, handwritten font. Buttons are bold, ink-styled text with hand-drawn box outlines.
component_rules.Scoreboard: Top-left absolute positioned panel. Styled like a ripped piece of masking tape or a sticky note. Displays 'Player 1 vs AI' score in Space Mono font.
component_rules.PowerMeter: Displayed during aiming. It should look like a physical plastic ruler or a hand-drawn ink bar that fills up next to the active pen.
component_rules.Buttons: No standard SaaS pill buttons. Use 'drawn' rectangles with heavy outlines. On hover, they should tilt slightly and scale up to mimic interacting with a physical piece of paper.
component_rules.Modals: MUST have solid non-transparent backgrounds (Paper color #F5F2EB). DO NOT use transparent backgrounds where content is under it.

motion.hover_states: Interactive paper elements tilt slightly (e.g., hover:-rotate-2 or hover:rotate-2) and scale up (hover:scale-105). Text color can switch from blue ink to red ink.
motion.entrance: Modals slide down from the top with a slight spring/bounce (simulating dropping paper onto a desk). Use framer-motion if possible, or CSS keyframes.
motion.transitions: Use specific properties (e.g., 'transition-transform 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)'). NEVER use 'transition-all'.

accessibility.contrast: Ensure ballpoint blue and red ink maintain at least 4.5:1 contrast against the paper background.
accessibility.focus: Focus states should mimic a bright yellow highlighter stroke behind the text (bg-[#F5D76E]).
accessibility.testing: All interactive and key informational elements MUST include a 'data-testid' attribute (e.g., data-testid='start-game-button', data-testid='mute-toggle', data-testid='player-score').

desk_background.description: Dark wooden desk texture to be used as the absolute background of the entire app/game viewport (`h-screen w-screen bg-cover bg-center`).

paper_texture.description: Ruled notebook paper texture to be used as a background image for the main menu modal and win/lose screens.

physics_libraries.recommendation: Use Matter.js for the 2D physics engine (pens, table bounds, friction, collisions). Render the physics world onto an HTML5 `<canvas>` that sits beneath the React UI shell.

instructions_to_main_agent: You are building a React-based UI shell overlaying a 2D physics game.
Focus purely on implementing the HTML/Tailwind shell using `.js` files (not TSX).
Import Google Fonts 'Caveat' and 'Space Mono' in your index.css.
Use Phosphor icons or Lucide React for UI icons, styled to look like ink sketches.
Render modals and HUD elements as absolute positioned elements on top of the 'desk' background container.
The UI is Diegetic: Every panel, button, and text should look like a physical object (paper, tape, ink) placed on the desk.
Ensure the mute toggle and difficulty selector clearly indicate their state.
UNIVERSAL_GUIDELINES_FOR_MAIN_AGENT: Do not converge toward generic 'AI slop' aesthetics. Avoid default centered layouts, simplistic gradients, and uniform styling.
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy. Drop shadows on paper elements are crucial to separate them from the desk.
Do not use complete transparent backgrounds for overlays/modals.
Do not apply 'transition: all'. Apply specific transitions like 'transition: transform 0.2s ease, opacity 0.2s ease'.
Do not center align the app container (.App { text-align: center; }). Keep natural reading flows.
Never use AI assistant Emoji characters like 🤖🧠💭 for icons.
Every interaction needs micro-animations - hover states, transitions, entrance animations. Static = dead.
